title: DataProtectionOfficer
description: GDPR-sourced archetype — data protection officer designation and properties under Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Articles 37-39 define when a DPO must be designated, required qualifications, independence guarantees, and tasks. Rootless — regulatory compliance dimension. Source: GDPR Articles 37, 38, 39.

dpoRequired.description: Whether DPO designation is mandatory. Required when: (a) processing is by a public authority/body (Art 37(1)(a)); (b) core activities require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale (Art 37(1)(b)); (c) core activities consist of large-scale processing of special categories or criminal conviction data (Art 37(1)(c)).

dpoDesignated.description: Whether a DPO has been designated. Source: GDPR Art 37(1).

dpoQualified.description: Whether the DPO is designated on the basis of professional qualities and expert knowledge of data protection law and practices. Source: GDPR Art 37(5).

dpoIndependent.description: Whether the DPO operates independently — does not receive instructions regarding the exercise of tasks, is not dismissed or penalised for performing tasks, and reports directly to highest management level. Source: GDPR Art 38(3).

dpoContactPublished.description: Whether the DPO contact details have been published and communicated to the supervisory authority. Source: GDPR Art 37(7).

dpoNoConflictOfInterest.description: Whether the DPO does not hold a position that leads to a conflict of interest with DPO tasks. Other tasks and duties must not result in a conflict of interest. Source: GDPR Art 38(6).

dpoResourcesProvided.description: Whether the controller/processor provides the DPO with resources necessary to carry out tasks and maintain expert knowledge. Source: GDPR Art 38(2).
